v4: one ensemble, full or compressed

Richard Aubrey White

Source: vignettes/v4.Rmd
v4.Rmd

The v4 nowcasts return a csfmt_ensemble_v4. The rate, trend, HLM and MEM steps take one and return it with their results added. A full ensemble holds draws in memory. A compressed ensemble holds a table with a point value and 9 percentiles for each base measure, and you store that table.

This vignette takes one simulated series from weekly counts to a stored table, and back again.

Build a full ensemble

The series has 320 weeks of positive tests out of all tests. Each week has 100 draws. Here they are simulated, but in a real run they come from a nowcast such as nowcast_ecdf_v4().

library(data.table)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'data.table'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     %notin%
library(csalert)
#> csalert 2026.10.18
#> https://niphr.github.io/csalert/

w <- cstime::dates_by_isoyearweek$isoyearweek
iyw <- w[match("2018-01", w) + 0:319]
season_week <- cstime::isoyearweek_to_seasonweek_n(iyw)
share <- 0.05 + 0.15 * exp(-(season_week - 25)^2 / 40)
set.seed(1)
tested <- matrix(rpois(320 * 100, 2000), nrow = 320)
positive <- matrix(rbinom(length(tested), tested, share), nrow = 320)

ens <- csfmt_ensemble_v4(
  data.table(location_code = "nation", isoyearweek = iyw),
  id_cols = "location_code",
  draws = list(positive = positive, tested = tested)
)
ens
#> <csfmt_ensemble_v4> full | 320 rows | 1 series | draws: positive, tested

Each draw matrix has one row per week and one column per draw. Column j is the same draw in every measure.

Add a rate, then run the trend and HLM 

ens <- ens_add_rate_v4(
  ens,
  numerator = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  per = 100,
  name = "positive_pr100"
)
ens <- short_term_trend_v4(
  ens,
  measure = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  name = "positive_pr100",
  seed = 4
)
ens <- signal_detection_hlm_v4(ens, measure = "positive_pr100")
ens$data[
  316:320,
  .(isoyearweek, positive_pr100_trend_pinc, positive_pr100_hlm_prob_high)
]
#>    isoyearweek positive_pr100_trend_pinc positive_pr100_hlm_prob_high
#>         <char>                     <num>                        <num>
#> 1:     2024-03                 0.9258002                         0.00
#> 2:     2024-04                 0.9228678                         0.00
#> 3:     2024-05                 0.9110528                         0.00
#> 4:     2024-06                 0.8697581                         0.08
#> 5:     2024-07                 0.7609514                         0.19

The trend models the counts of positive in a quasi-Poisson regression, with the log of tested as the offset. positive_pr100_trend_pinc is P(increasing). The HLM step compares each draw of the rate with a limit from the 5 earlier years. positive_pr100_hlm_prob_high is the share of the draws at or above that limit.

Compress to a table 

stored <- ens_compress_v4(ens)
dim(stored)
#> [1] 320  49
max(nchar(names(stored), type = "bytes"))
#> [1] 29

The table holds the columns of $data. It also holds a median and 9 percentiles for each of the 3 base measures, positive, tested and positive_pr100. It holds no draws, and each column is a plain vector. ens_compress_v4() stops with an error when a name is longer than 63 bytes, the limit of a PostgreSQL name. So you can write the table to PostgreSQL.

Read the table back and run a step again 

back <- as_ensemble_v4(stored, id_cols = "location_code", n_sim = 100)
back
#> <csfmt_ensemble_v4> compressed | 320 rows | 1 series | draws: none
back <- short_term_trend_v4(
  back,
  measure = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  name = "positive_pr100",
  seed = 4
)
pinc <- data.table(
  isoyearweek = iyw,
  full = ens$data$positive_pr100_trend_pinc,
  rebuilt = back$data$positive_pr100_trend_pinc
)
pinc[316:320]
#>    isoyearweek      full   rebuilt
#>         <char>     <num>     <num>
#> 1:     2024-03 0.9258002 0.9482298
#> 2:     2024-04 0.9228678 0.9435558
#> 3:     2024-05 0.9110528 0.9488082
#> 4:     2024-06 0.8697581 0.9351281
#> 5:     2024-07 0.7609514 0.8329660
max(abs(pinc$full - pinc$rebuilt), na.rm = TRUE)
#> [1] 0.1095947

Each step rebuilds the draws of the base measures that it reads, from the stored percentiles, with seed 4. n_sim = 100 gives the same number of draws as the full ensemble. The rebuild is an approximation. On this series, the two P(increasing) values differ by at most 0.11 over the 318 weeks that have a trend.

Before a step on a rate, add the rate again from its parts. A step that rebuilds the rate from its own percentiles loses the pairing of its draws with the draws of positive and tested.

back <- ens_add_rate_v4(
  back,
  numerator = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  per = 100,
  name = "positive_pr100"
)
back <- signal_detection_hlm_v4(back, measure = "positive_pr100")
back
#> <csfmt_ensemble_v4> compressed | 320 rows | 1 series | draws: positive_pr100_trend_beta1, positive_pr100_trend_se, positive_pr100, positive_pr100_hlm
